meta.titre: Forming adverbs of manner from adjectives

sections.contenu_markdown: A verb never takes an adjective directly: it needs an adverb, its natural partner.

items: Distinction between adjectives and verbs in a sentence

sections.contenu_markdown: Most English adverbs of manner are formed by adding '-ly' to the adjective (honest → honestly, careful → carefully). Adverbs modify verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs, while adjectives modify nouns only.

sections.enonce_markdown: Complete: My sister spoke ... about the matter in court (honest).
sections.conclusion_markdown: My sister spoke honestly about the matter in court.

items.erreur_markdown: Using the adjective form directly after a verb ('spoke honest').
items.pourquoi_faux: Adjectives cannot modify verbs in standard English; only adverbs can.
items.correction_markdown: Always check whether the word being modified is a verb (needs adverb) or a noun (needs adjective).

items_markdown: Verbs are modified by adverbs, not adjectives
Most adverbs of manner = adjective + ly
